title: Affine-to-global pro-etale cohomology bound over a zero-dimensional affine base
statement:
Let $B$ be an affine scheme every prime of whose coordinate ring is maximal, and let $g:X\to B$ be a separated morphism of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix integers $e,a\geq0$. Suppose every geometric fibre $X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$, for every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to B$ with $K$ algebraically closed, has topological Krull dimension at most $e$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathcal R$ be any commutative ring object in abelian sheaves on the small pro-etale site of $X$, and let $M$ be an ordinary internal $\mathcal R$-module [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use the small-site and indexing universes of [def-weil-size-convention].
For an open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, restriction means restriction of the ring and module to the open slice, viewed on $V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$; denote them by $\mathcal R|_V$ and $M|_V$ [def-weil-open-immersion, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison]. Suppose that for every affine open subscheme $V\subseteq X$,
$$H^q\bigl(R\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M|_V)\bigr)=0\qquad(q>a).$$
Then
$$H^r\bigl(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M)\bigr)=0\qquad(r>e+a).$$
In these formulas $R\Gamma$ is the ordinary right-derived global-section functor in the indicated internal module category, computed by an injective resolution with the module in degree zero; values are in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. No constructibility, adic completeness, coefficient restriction, Noetherianity, or finite presentation is assumed. Neither $B$ being w-contractible nor separable closedness of its residue fields is required. The empty scheme is included.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral (spectral-space cohomology above dimension); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0732, lemma-Leray (ringed-topos Leray spectral sequence). Agent-formulated affine-to-global consequence, with dimension read from the zero-dimensional-base fibres. Blueprint application: refinement proof (2), local geometric heart estimate.

proof.text: Since $B$ is affine and $g$ is separated and of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes $X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] makes $|X|$ spectral. In particular it is sober: each nonempty irreducible closed subset has a generic point, by [def-weil-spectral-space].

For every $b\in B$, the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_b$ is separated and of finite type over $\kappa(b)$ by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(b)}$. The field-extension clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] gives $\dim X_b=\dim(X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\overline{\kappa(b)})$. By [def-weil-geometric-fibre] this base change is the geometric fibre in the hypothesis, so $\dim X_b\leq e$. This also covers empty fibres.

Consider a chain $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_n$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $X$. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $Z_n$ supplied in step 1, and put $b=g(\eta)$. Every point of $B$ is closed: under $B\cong\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)$ its prime ideal is maximal. Continuity gives $g(Z_n)=g(\overline{\{\eta\}})\subseteq\overline{\{b\}}=\{b\}$. Thus every $Z_i$ lies in $g^{-1}(b)$. It remains closed and irreducible in that subspace, with the same strict inclusions. The homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] turns this into a chain of length $n$ in $X_b$, so $n\leq e$ by step 2. Taking the supremum of chain lengths, as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], gives $\dim X\leq e$. If $X$ is empty the supremum is $-\infty$ and the same inequality holds.

source.place: Tag 01K1, lemma-fibre-topological; elementary chain argument using Topology Tag 0055.

proof.text: First identify the internal $\mathcal R$-module category with sectionwise modules over its reconstructed commutative ring sheaf, using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] for the tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The site and coefficients are in the common universe of the statement. The equivalence leaves section groups and restrictions unchanged. It preserves kernels, cokernels and monomorphisms by their universal properties; the injective lifting condition is preserved by its fully faithful inverse. Thus it identifies injective resolutions and their evaluated complexes, hence the right-derived section groups. The same reasoning applies on each open slice, where the equivalence still leaves the restricted sheaves unchanged.

source.place: Tag 00YV, algebraic structures in sheaves; elementary transport of injective resolutions along the indicated equivalence.

proof.text: Using the identification in step 4, put $F=M_{ab}$ on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$. The small skeleton and coefficient universe are those in the statement. For this site and each open slice, [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] give enough injectives in modules over the actual restricted ring. Apply [lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice] to $M$ at the terminal object and to $M|_V$ at the terminal object of each open slice. The open localization [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] and actual-ring comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison] identify these slices and coefficients with $V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, $\mathcal R|_V$ and $M|_V$. Hence the module-derived groups in the statement identify with $H^q(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},F)$ and $H^q(V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},F|_V)$. In particular the latter are zero for every affine $V$ and $q>a$. This uses the arbitrary-ring-sheaf comparison, not a constant-coefficient specialization; injectivity after forgetting scalars is not asserted.

source.place: Tags 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, and 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open; proetale.tex open localization.

proof.text: Compose $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}\to X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] with $X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\to X_{\rm Zar}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites], using [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]. Denote the composite by $\epsilon$. Its defining continuous functor sends an open $V$ to the same $X$-scheme $V$, so $(\epsilon_*F)(V)=F(V)$; it preserves the terminal object. On abelian sheaves $\epsilon^{-1}$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact].

source.place: Tags 00X6, proposition-get-morphism, and 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites; sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC.

proof.text: For $q\geq0$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] identifies $R^q\epsilon_*F$ with the Zariski sheafification of $V\mapsto H^q(V,F)$, where $V$ is the pro-etale object over $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization] and [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], this value is $H^q(V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},F|_V)$. For $q>a$ it is zero on affine opens by step 5. These form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. On any open, every presheaf section therefore restricts to zero on an affine cover. For any Zariski sheaf $G$, every presheaf morphism from this presheaf to $G$ is zero, since its image on any section restricts to zero on an affine cover and $G$ is separated. Thus the zero sheaf has the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and the associated sheaf is zero. Consequently $R^q\epsilon_*F=0$ for $q>a$.

source.place: Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images; Tag 03F3; schemes.tex Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens.

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to $\epsilon_*:\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}})\to\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\rm Zar})$ and $\Gamma(X_{\rm Zar},-)$. The source and intermediate categories are Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] with the constant integer ring; the target $\operatorname{Ab}$ is the same construction on the one-object trivial site. These functors are additive and left exact. Since $\epsilon_*$ is right adjoint to the exact $\epsilon^{-1}$ of step 6, [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] says it sends injectives to injectives, hence to global-section-acyclics by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2). Evaluation at the terminal object gives $\Gamma(X_{\rm Zar},\epsilon_*(-))=\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},-)$. We obtain a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(X_{\rm Zar},R^q\epsilon_*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},F)$.

source.place: Tag 0732, lemma-Leray, specialized to abelian sheaves (the constant integer ring); derived.tex Tag 015N.

proof.text: The space $|X|$ is spectral by step 1 and has dimension at most $e$ by step 3. For each $q\geq0$, apply [lem-sfb-spectral-space-cohomology-dimension] to the abelian Zariski sheaf $R^q\epsilon_*F$. This gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $p>e$. Step 7 gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $q>a$. Thus the entire $E_2$ page is supported in the rectangle $0\leq p\leq e$, $0\leq q\leq a$.

If $r>e+a$ and $p+q=r$ with $p,q\geq0$, either $p>e$ or $q>a$, so $E_2^{p,q}=0$. Each later term at that bidegree is a subquotient of the preceding one and is therefore zero. The first-quadrant convergence in step 8 gives a finite exhaustive separated filtration of $H^r(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},F)$ whose associated graded terms are these zero $E_\infty^{p,r-p}$. Induction through the finite filtration makes the abutment zero. The terminal-object identification of step 5 gives exactly $H^r(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M))=0$ as required. The argument applies to $e=0$ and $a=0$; for $X=\varnothing$, sections and their derived groups are zero as well.

source.place: Tag 0732, elementary rectangle-vanishing consequence of first-quadrant convergence.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NM-37de593d9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 10 steps, the new node and every cited statement. Item statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are byte-identical to the base copy in the NA snapshot, so the target is not weakened. New node lem-sfb-spectral-space-cohomology-dimension is exactly Stacks cohomology.tex 0A3G(1) (Scheiderer; 'dimension at most d' is equivalent to 'dimension d'). Tested on the empty space, profinite spaces (dim 0) and Spec of a DVR. Searched the DAG for 0A3G, 02UZ and spectral-space cohomology: every hit is Noetherian or unrelated, so there is no duplicate, and a Noetherian bound could not be applied to the possibly non-Noetherian base anyway. Route checks: step 1 shows X is qcqs, hence spectral and sober. Steps 2-3 give dim X <= e from the field-extension clause of lem-kun-dimension-extension and the elementary chain argument, using closed points of B and the homeomorphism clause of def-pc-scheme-fibre. Steps 4-5 compare internal modules with the arbitrary-ring sectionwise modules, then with underlying abelian cohomology through lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice, the weakly-etale localization and the ringed open comparison. The equivalence node's 'local equivalences are monoidal' hypothesis follows in one line from clause 1 of sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor (strong monoidal sheafification); I accepted that as elementary. Step 6: nu is a morphism of sites because its left adjoint preserves finite limits; composing it with the Zariski-etale morphism by 03CB gives the composite with exact pullback. Step 7: R^q epsilon_* F is the sheafification of a presheaf that is locally zero on the affine basis, and it vanishes by the universal property of sheafification. Step 8: Grothendieck spectral sequence, injectives preserved by the right adjoint. Steps 9-10: the rectangle argument. All 26 declared split_report.tool_uses are generic inputs (site, sheaf, dimension and spectral-sequence tools); accepted. No SGA citation. Not a re-split item. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem proEtale_cohomology_vanishes_of_affine_of_zeroDimensional_base {B X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine B] (hB : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(B, ⊤), p.asIdeal.IsMaximal) (g : X ⟶ B) [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] (e a : ℕ) (he : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ B), topologicalKrullDim (pullback g b : Scheme.{u}) ≤ (e : WithBot ℕ∞)) (R : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj R] [IsCommMonObj R] (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) R) (hlocal : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → ∀ q : ℕ, a < q → IsZero (((Mod.forget R ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1} ⋙ (evaluation X.ProEtᵒᵖ Ab.{u + 1}).obj (op (Scheme.ProEt.mk U.ι))).rightDerived q).obj M)) (r : ℕ) (hr : e + a < r) : IsZero (((Mod.forget R ⋙ sheafToPresheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1} ⋙ (evaluation X.ProEtᵒᵖ Ab.{u + 1}).obj (op (Scheme.ProEt.mk (𝟙 X)))).rightDerived r).obj M)
lean.note: The q-th ordinary module-derived sections of an open slice are rendered by the q-th rightDerived of internal-module evaluation at its pro-etale open object. The internal/sectionwise module equivalence, module-derived evaluation slice comparison, and actual-ring open comparison identify this with RΓ(V_proet,M|V). Evaluation is derived in the internal R-module category, not after forgetting to the abelian-sheaf category. Nonnegative degrees are sufficient since a,e ≥ 0.
